description: i18n (next-intl: es default, nl, en fallback), PWA (Serwist manifest + service worker + offline fallback), and final navigation/empty-state polish. Depends on all previous FEATs (needs real pages/login/dashboards to translate and a stable route tree to precache). This is the last feature before the cross-FEAT integration/review loop.
steps: Install next-intl's build plugin wiring: wrap next.config.ts with `next-intl/plugin`'s default export (`createNextIntlPlugin()` or the exact exported name from node_modules/next-intl/dist/types/plugin — confirm the exact API by reading that file before writing code, per AGENTS.md) around the existing config (which already has images.remotePatterns and will also get withSerwistInit in this same FEAT — compose both wrappers).

Create src/i18n/request.ts exporting `getRequestConfig(async ({requestLocale}) => { ... return { locale, messages } })` from 'next-intl/server', reading the active locale from a cookie (e.g. NEXT_LOCALE) with fallback: if a cookie is present and valid use it, else fall back to the signed-in user's User.locale (accountant default 'nl', client default 'es' per the task — set this default at Credentials-authorize/user-creation time in FEAT-002/FEAT-001, not here; here just read whatever User.locale or cookie says), else 'en'. Do NOT implement prefix-based [locale] URL routing — this app uses /admin and /app role-based paths, not localized paths, per the context.json decision.

Create messages/es.json, messages/nl.json, messages/en.json with keys for at least: login page (title, email label, password label, submit, error), client dashboard (nav/empty states), admin panel (nav/empty states, invite form labels, review panel labels). Keep the key structure flat-namespaced (e.g. { "Login": { "title": ... }, "AdminClients": {...} }) consistent with how useTranslations(namespace) will be called.

Wrap the root layout (src/app/layout.tsx) with `NextIntlClientProvider` (from 'next-intl', the client-safe re-export confirmed in node_modules/next-intl/dist/types/react-server/index.d.ts and the client equivalent) so Client Components (login form, admin clients UI) can call useTranslations. Pass messages/locale down from the Server Component layout via `getLocale()`/`getMessages()` from 'next-intl/server'.

Replace the hardcoded Spanish/English UI strings in src/app/login/page.tsx and the admin/client pages built in FEAT-002/003/004 with `useTranslations('Namespace')` calls backed by the new message files, for at minimum: login page and one admin + one client dashboard view (the task's acceptance bar is 'renders at least login/dashboard with translated messages', not a full audit of every string).

Add a basic language selector (a simple <select> or three links) that sets the NEXT_LOCALE cookie and reloads/refreshes the current route — can live in a shared layout/header component used by both /admin and /app sections.

Add Serwist: install devDependency `serwist` is already present per package.json; wrap next.config.ts with `withSerwistInit({ swSrc: 'src/app/sw.ts', swDest: 'public/sw.js' })` (composed with the next-intl wrapper from this same FEAT — apply both HOFs around the base NextConfig object). Create src/app/sw.ts per the confirmed @serwist/next 9.5.13 pattern (defaultCache from '@serwist/next/worker', Serwist from 'serwist', self.__SW_MANIFEST, serwist.addEventListeners()) with a basic offline fallback entry pointing at a new src/app/offline/page.tsx (simple static 'you are offline' page).

Create app/manifest.ts (TypeScript, App Router metadata route) returning a MetadataRoute.Manifest per node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/01-metadata/manifest.md: name/short_name/description for the Ledger OCR app, start_url '/', display 'standalone', and at least one icon entry (reuse an existing icon in public/ if present, else add a minimal placeholder SVG/PNG — do not spend effort on real branding, a functional manifest is the bar).

Add tsconfig.json types for Serwist per its getting-started guide: add '@serwist/next/typings' to compilerOptions.types and 'webworker' to compilerOptions.lib, and exclude 'public/sw.js' — merge into the existing tsconfig.json without removing current settings (paths alias, existing lib array, etc).

Polish navigation: src/app/page.tsx (currently default create-next-app content) becomes a thin Server Component that calls auth() and redirects '/' -> '/login' (no session), '/admin' (ACCOUNTANT), or '/app' (CLIENT) — this is distinct from proxy.ts's route-protection role, this is the root-path landing redirect. Add reasonable empty states (e.g. 'no expenses yet', 'no clients invited yet') to the list views built in FEAT-002/003/004 if they don't already have one.

Run `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build` and confirm the build output includes the service worker generation step without errors and that app/manifest.ts and src/app/offline/page.tsx are both listed as routes. Then a short-lived start+curl smoke test: curl / unauthenticated and confirm a redirect to /login; curl /manifest.json (or whatever path Next serves app/manifest.ts at) and confirm valid JSON; curl /sw.js and confirm it's served from public/; then kill the server.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` succeeds with both next-intl and Serwist wrapping next.config.ts active (no plugin-composition errors)
Visiting /login with no NEXT_LOCALE cookie and no session renders Spanish (default) copy from messages/es.json; switching the locale selector to 'nl' or 'en' changes the rendered copy
app/manifest.ts is served as a valid web app manifest (confirmed via a request against the built app) and public/sw.js is generated by the build without breaking next build
GET / with no session redirects to /login; with an ACCOUNTANT session redirects to /admin; with a CLIENT session redirects to /app
`npm run lint` and `npx tsc --noEmit` both pass
verification: `npm run build` — succeeds; output includes app/manifest route, src/app/offline route, and Serwist's service worker build step with no errors

Short-lived `npm run start` + curl: `curl -i http://localhost:3000/` unauthenticated expects a redirect (3xx) to /login; `curl -i http://localhost:3000/manifest.json` (or `.webmanifest`, confirm actual path from manifest.ts/next build output) expects 200 + valid JSON; `curl -i http://localhost:3000/sw.js` expects 200; then kill the server, confirm nothing left running

Visual/content check (read the rendered message files and the page source, or curl + grep for a known translated string) confirming es/nl/en message keys used on the login page actually resolve to different text per locale
findings: Implemented and verified in the task's final review pass (review.json verdict APPROVED): next-intl (es default, nl, en) wired via src/i18n/request.ts and next.config.ts composed with withSerwistInit; messages/es.json, nl.json, en.json cover Login/ClientHome/ClientExpenses/AdminHome/AdminClients/AdminCategories/ReviewPanel/AccountStatus namespaces; root layout wraps children in NextIntlClientProvider; Serwist PWA (src/app/sw.ts, app/manifest.ts, src/app/offline/page.tsx) builds cleanly with the service worker bundled at /sw.js scope '/'; root src/app/page.tsx redirects by role. npm run lint, npx tsc --noEmit, and npm run build all passed with all 21 expected routes generated, including /manifest.webmanifest and /offline.
